data.title: Clobetasol propionate 0.05% (ointment, lotion, solution)
data.summary: IV Topical corticosteroids · Super-potent fluorinated steroid (US class 1; UK 'very potent')
data.body:
_Topicals · IV Topical corticosteroids_

**Class:** Super-potent fluorinated steroid (US class 1; UK 'very potent')

## Mechanism of action
- Most potent glucocorticoid receptor agonist used on skin — strong anti-inflammatory and antiproliferative effects

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Chronic plaque psoriasis (body; scalp — lotion/solution/shampoo), palmoplantar psoriasis and eczema
- Lichen planus (hypertrophic), lichen simplex chronicus, discoid lupus
- Lichen sclerosus (first-line, including genital — even in children under specialist care)
- Localised bullous pemphigoid (whole-body clobetasol is as effective as oral steroids)
- Alopecia areata (under occlusion), vitiligo (limited areas, short pulses)

## Dose & formulations
- Once or twice daily; maximum 50 g per week; usually no more than 2 weeks continuously, then taper or use pulsed/weekend therapy
- Bullous pemphigoid: 10–40 g/day initially over the whole body (except face), then taper over months
- Lichen sclerosus: once daily for 1 month, alternate days for 1 month, twice weekly for 1 month, then as needed

## Adverse effects
- All topical steroid side effects — most likely with this agent: atrophy, striae, purpura, telangiectasia, steroid rosacea, tinea incognito, HPA suppression with large areas, Cushing syndrome
- Commonly misused in India in fairness and 'itch' creams — leading cause of topical steroid-damaged face

## Contraindications
- Face, flexures, genitals (except lichen sclerosus), children under 12 (except specialist use)
- Rosacea, acne, perioral dermatitis, untreated infection

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid large areas/long courses (association with low birth weight).

## Viva points
- Most potent topical steroid: max 50 g/week, 2 weeks
- First-line for lichen sclerosus and localised bullous pemphigoid
- Ointment more potent than cream; lotion/solution for scalp

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.45; Khopkar ch.22. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
